Senses.Explanation: This is the work of appraising and commenting on old cases or verses, and the same term labels the commentary produced by that work. Chan books make it a named layer of case literature: the named commentator addresses earlier verses, and the resulting appraisal-commentary can become a titled collection. Title constructions name Yuanwu Keqin appraising Xuedou Chongxian's verses, Wansong Xingxiu appraising Hongzhi Zhengjue's verses, and Linquan Conglun appraising verses associated with Touzi Yiqing and Danxia Zichun. Daguan Zhenke's signed preface to the Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wushan Jingduan gives the documentary sequence: 'from recorded encounters, verses on old cases were made; from verses on old cases, appraisal-commentary collections were made' (由機緣而頌古作，由頌古而評唱集). A poem heading by Guxue Zhenzhe speaks of 'burning Wansong's appraisal-commentary on public cases' (焚萬松評唱公案). Its verbal, nominal, and title constructions are grammatical deployments of the same activity and product, not separate dictionary senses.
Senses.Note: One sense under item 8: noun, verb, and title-modifier constructions name the same appraisal-commentary work, while an attached comment, a substitute response, laying down a response, composing a verse on an old case, and picking up an old case are different devices.
